title: Choir and Hollow
premise: Wendell Marchetti has spent his life in Hollowvale, a valley warded against magic, where his gift for speaking with beasts must stay hidden. When the old gods resume answering prayers and the wards begin to fail, he is dragged beyond the valley's edge into a world where the covenant binding gods, beasts, and mortals has quietly rotted. Guided by a disgraced priestess and the god who remembers him, Wendell must reforge the covenant at the Hollow Altar before the realms unravel. He succeeds, but only by surrendering the valley's safety forever — and choosing love and belonging in the wide, dangerous world over the survival he was raised to guard.
about_author: Odile Almeida is the pen name of a former choir director who left a coastal cathedral town to write full-time, trading hymnals for grimoires. Her work is known for quiet, aching fantasy where faith and family are the hardest magics of all.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In Hollowvale, Wendell secretly soothes a dying ewe with borrowed words, revealing his beast-speaker gift to no one but the shepherd's daughter, Sable. The valley's wards hum strangely that night. The emotional beat is the ache of a gift with no audience — belonging to a place that would fear him if it knew.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A traveler dies at the valley gate, and his last prayer is audibly answered — the first magic inside Hollowvale in three generations. The wards crack like river ice. Wendell's grandmother makes him swear to stay silent, but the beasts have begun speaking back, urgent and afraid. Beat: dread blooming under routine.

chapters.title: The Priestess of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Sable's estranged aunt, the disgraced priestess Maren, arrives seeking the valley's hidden godstone. She recognizes what Wendell is and offers to teach him — if he leaves with her. His grandmother forbids it. Beat: the first fork in the road, love of home versus the pull of purpose.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Remember
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The valley's animals, led by an ancient blind mule, tell Wendell the truth: Hollowvale wasn't a refuge, it was a prison built to hide the covenant's keystone — him. The wards were made to cage his bloodline. Beat: devastating reframe; the home that sheltered him was built to bury him.

chapters.title: Leaving Hollowvale
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable chooses to go with Wendell, defying her family, as the wards fail fully and magic floods the valley. They slip out at dawn past the old godstone while Maren holds the gate against something hunting them from the god-side. Beat: grief and exhilaration entwined; home is now a place they can never return to as they were.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On the pilgrim road, they find villages bargaining with half-awakened gods for scraps of favor, each prayer a small theft from the dying covenant. Wendell learns his voice can quiet the gods — and that they want him for it. Beat: wonder curdling into manipulation; everyone wants to use him, including Maren.

chapters.title: The God Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In a drowned chapel, Wendell meets Vesper, the forgotten god who has watched his bloodline since before the valley existed. Vesper reveals the covenant broke because the last beast-speaker refused the altar's price. Wendell and Sable confess their love; duty and desire collide. Beat: tenderness sharpened by the knowledge that one of them will pay.

chapters.title: The Hunted Pilgrimage
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The god who broke the covenant — the Hollow One, who feeds on unanswered prayers — hunts them across the high moors. Maren is taken buying them time. Sable, mortal and magicless, must find her own worth in a story that keeps demanding Wendell sacrifice himself. Beat: fierce, defiant love; refusing to be the one left behind.

chapters.title: The Hollow Altar
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. At the Altar, the price is revealed: a covenant needs a voice willing to be silenced. Wendell prepares to give up his gift — his self — but Sable offers her mortality instead, and Vesper offers godhood's end. The Hollow One attacks mid-rite. Beat: climax; three sacrifices colliding, and Wendell refusing every version of the bargain that costs someone else.

chapters.title: A Voice for Every Living Thing
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell rewrites the covenant: not one silenced voice, but all voices shared — gods, beasts, and mortals bound in mutual answerability, with the Hollow One given a place at the choir rather than exile. The valley opens forever. He and Sable build a life between realms, teachers of the new covenant. Beat: bittersweet resolution; survival's price was safety, and they paid it gladly.
